algorithm.Title: Nasal Allergies (Hay Fever) - Male (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Male
Definition: Hay fever / nasal allergy assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for lip/mouth/throat/tongue swelling, breathing/swallowing difficulty, faintness, confusion, floppiness, or collapse. Use the person's prescribed adrenaline auto-injector immediately according to its instructions and emergency plan; antihistamine must not delay adrenaline or 999. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
algorithm.Author: IST Health Open-Source Guideline Content
algorithm.LastRevised: RESEARCH_REQUIRED - internal IST clinical adaptation date is not recorded

questions.Question: Are throat or tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, faintness, confusion, or collapse the main concern?
questions.Information: Systemic allergic-reaction features require the Anaphylaxis pathway.

questions.Question: Is there sudden swelling of the lips, mouth, throat, or tongue, or severe difficulty breathing?
questions.Information: Universal emergency rule-out added ahead of the hay fever guidance itself - typical hay fever does not cause airway swelling or severe breathing difficulty, so these signs suggest a different, more serious allergic reaction.

questions.Question: Are symptoms getting worse, or have pharmacy medicines not improved them?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance: see a doctor if symptoms are worsening or pharmacy treatments haven't helped - may be referred for immunotherapy.

questions.Question: Is this typical hay fever with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance: a pharmacist can recommend antihistamines and steroid nasal sprays for typical hay fever.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency allergy response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for lip/mouth/throat/tongue swelling, breathing/swallowing difficulty, faintness, confusion, floppiness, or collapse. Use the person's prescribed adrenaline auto-injector immediately according to its instructions and emergency plan; antihistamine must not delay adrenaline or 999. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: breathing or swallowing worsens; swelling spreads; faintness, floppiness, confusion, or collapse.

advice.Title: Routine hay fever follow-up
Content: Book a clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) if symptoms worsen or pharmacy treatments aren't helping.
Call Back If: symptoms significantly worsen.

advice.Title: Governed hay-fever care
Content: Reduce pollen exposure with closed windows when counts are high, shower/change after outdoor exposure, and use wraparound glasses. Antihistamine, eye-drop, and nasal-spray selection/dose require age/weight, pregnancy/breastfeeding, asthma, glaucoma/urinary/cardiac conditions, sedation and driving/aviation duties, technique, and current-medicine checks under the approved Qatar pathway.
Call Back If: symptoms worsen despite treatment; wheeze, asthma deterioration, facial swelling, eye pain, or visual change.

references: NHS.UK, "Hay fever", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/hay-fever/ (page last reviewed 21 March 2024)

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What is the person's exact age and sex, are they pregnant/breastfeeding, immunocompromised, asthmatic, or in a safety-critical driving/aviation role, and how long have symptoms lasted? Confirm no anaphylaxis, serious asthma, infection, eye pain, or visual change.
